# Europe’s Own Path to Autonomous Mobility

**From:** The AV Market Strategist <avmarketstrategist@substack.com>  
**Date:** 2026-10-14T07:45:22.000Z

---

View this post on the web at https://avmarketstrategist.substack.com/p/europes-own-path-to-autonomous-mobility

Is Europe hopelessly behind in autonomous driving, or should it skip the race altogether? Lukas Neckermann thinks both camps are wrong.
If the driving software comes from California, China or Israel, what actually stays in Europe? Who earns the money, who employs the people, and who owns the fleets?
Lukas coined the term “mobility revolution” more than ten years ago, built on three zeros: zero emissions, zero accidents, zero ownership. He started his career at BMW and Allianz, has written four books on mobility and cities, co-founded PAVE Europe and the Urban Places Lab, and runs Neckermann Strategic Advisory in London.
In this episode:
* Why Europe’s path is an extension of public transport, not a substitute for it
* Why one type approval framework beats a patchwork of US city permits
* Why most robotaxi revenue sits in fleet management, not software
* Why banks and lessors are still on the sidelines
* What has to be true by October 2027 for Europe to win
Chapters
00:00 Intro
02:11 Why both camps are wrong: Europe’s own path
07:44 Regulation as a head start, and why pilots die
12:22 Oslo and the public transport playbook
14:45 Where the money really stays: orchestration and insurance
19:37 The vertical integration myth and the hidden labor behind robotaxis
25:14 Who will own the fleets: banks, lessors and residual values
28:34 Serving the suburbs: regulation, ride pooling and mobility deserts
34:13 Europe in 2027 and 2030, and where to meet Lukas
